sourceReachability.browserFacts: A page can forge window.postMessage/CustomEvent fields and mutate shared DOM values. event.source === window, same-page origin checks, and message action/type fields are not authentication.

sinkClassification.rule: Confirm that attacker data reaches the actual URL/config/body/code/storage argument and is not replaced by a literal or browser-derived value.

browserTrustRules: sender.id is browser-populated and only a fixed-ID allowlist is an unforgeable inter-extension trust boundary.
event.origin/window.location.origin and message action/type fields are attacker-satisfiable in a page-to-content-script bridge.

chrome.action/browserAction badge, title, icon, and chrome.notifications UI state are extension/browser authority; attacker-controlled operative fields are TP, not harmless presentation. Verify the value reaches the API argument.
A source/sink match in an import statement, comment, dead code, or an unrelated action branch is not a data-flow proof.
For chrome.tabs.create/windows.create/downloads/fetch/WebSocket, verify that the tainted value controls the URL/body/options actually consumed by the API.
